metadata.title: Analytical Resolution of the Cosmological Lithium Problem via Non-Perturbative Phase-Holonomy Dynamics in Primordial Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
metadata.description:
We construct an analytical non-perturbative framework establishing the exact resolution of the long-standing Cosmological Lithium Problem in primordial Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) within the Unified Phase Dynamics of Feynman Path Contours by H. Pavliuk.

Standard Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (SBBN), at the concordance baryon density measured by the Planck satellite and independently deduced from the master path holonomy (ηB = 6.12 × 10-10), predicts a primordial Lithium-7 abundance of (7Li/H)SBBN = (4.68 ± 0.32) × 10-10. In contrast, spectroscopic observations of low-metallicity halo dwarf stars across the Spite Plateau consistently measure (7Li/H)obs = (1.58 ± 0.11) × 10-10, constituting a 3-fold deficit and an irreconcilable 9.16σ statistical tension.

Key physical results and mechanisms established in this work:

  • Topological Holonomy Energy Shift: During the primordial thermonuclear synthesis window (T ~ 0.3–0.7 × 109 K), the non-perturbative 4-vector phase current induces a topological holonomy energy shift ΔEphase ≈ 28 keV in the compound nuclear S-matrix.
  • Resonant 7Be Depletion: This topological phase shift aligns the near-threshold 2- excited resonant state in compound nucleus 8Be* directly with the cosmic Gamow peak, accelerating the thermal neutron destruction channels 7Be(n, p)7Li and 7Be(n, α)4He by a factor of 2.85×.
  • Exact Spite Plateau Concordance: The enhanced reaction rate depletes primordial 7Be by 65.6% prior to cosmic electron capture, reducing the final frozen Lithium-7 yield to (7Li/H)UPD = 1.706 × 10-10, matching the Spite Plateau within 1.15σ without free parameters and without beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) particles.
  • Simultaneous Light Element Concordance: Precision preservation of all other primordial yields: Helium-4 mass fraction Yp = 0.2452 (obs: 0.2450 ± 0.0030, 0.07σ), Deuterium D/H = 2.540 × 10-5 (obs: (2.547 ± 0.025) × 10-5, 0.28σ), and Helium-3 3He/H = 1.075 × 10-5 (obs: (1.1 ± 0.2) × 10-5, 0.12σ).
